pr.title: Eliminate `UbChecks` for non-standard libraries
pr.description:
The purpose of this PR is to allow other passes to treat `UbChecks` as constants in MIR for optimization after #122629.

r? RalfJung
pr.author: dianqk

evidence: The purpose of this PR is to allow other passes to treat `UbChecks` as constants in MIR for optimization after #122629.
`#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]` prevents the designated crate from evaluating whether UB checks are enabled when optimizing MIR
flags: if the crate has debug assertions enabled or carries the `#[rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The dangerous/incorrect rewrite is to simplify `UbChecks` unconditionally to the current crate's `debug_assertions` value. That ignores `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`: standard-library crates built without debug assertions must keep `UbChecks` delayed so that monomorphization into a downstream crate with debug assertions still enables runtime UB checks. The PR guards the rewrite with `if !preserve_ub_checks { ctx.simplify_ub_check(...) }`. Correct transformation: replace only `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, _)` with `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Constant(...))` whose value is `Const::from_bool(tcx, tcx.sess.opts.debug_assertions)`, and skip this when the crate has `rustc_preserve_ub_checks`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR assignment statements containing `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, _)`, especially after inlining UB-check helpers such as `unreachable_unchecked::precondition_check` and `core::ub_checks::check_language_ub`. Relevant crate configurations include `-Cdebug-assertions=no`/`=yes` and presence or absence of `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`; the regression test uses `-Cdebug-assertions=no -Zinline-mir`.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `UbChecks` was a MIR nullary operation whose comment said it "Returns whether we want to check for UB. This returns the value of `cfg!(debug_assertions)` at monomorphization time." InstSimplify did not rewrite it, so MIR retained `_4 = UbChecks();` followed by `assume(_4);`, preventing constant propagation through UB-check branches in code such as inlined `unwrap_unchecked`.
pitfalls: Do not simplify `UbChecks` in crates carrying `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`; doing so would freeze the standard library's no-debug-assertions setting and lose runtime UB checks when linked/monomorphized into user crates with debug assertions.
Do not confuse `UbChecks` with `cfg!(debug_assertions)` evaluated at source level: the intrinsic is intentionally delayed until monomorphization, and the attribute exists to preserve that delay.
The replacement must produce `const false` when `-Cdebug-assertions=no`, as shown by the regression test expecting `_4 = const false; assume(_4);`, not merely delete the `assume`.

Other MIR output tests may change because duplicate switch targets and unreachable UB-check blocks can disappear after the constant is exposed; update expectations only where the new constant assignment actually justifies it.
A retained test name or old comment does not prove a replacement pass is wrong; compare the actual value assignment (`UbChecks()` versus `const false`).
preconditions: The crate being optimized does not contain the crate-level attribute `rustc_preserve_ub_checks`.
The replacement constant uses the optimizer's crate compilation setting `tcx.sess.opts.debug_assertions`, not a hardcoded `false` or `true`.
The preserved span/source info from the original statement is used for the new `ConstOperand`, keeping diagnostics tied to the `UbChecks` site.
analysis.summary: InstSimplify now replaces MIR `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, _)` with a boolean constant derived from `tcx.sess.opts.debug_assertions`, but only when the crate does not carry `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`. This lets downstream/other MIR passes treat UB-check gating as a constant, while preserving delayed evaluation for standard-library crates.
analysis.testStrategy: Add an `InstSimplify` MIR-opt unit test, e.g. `tests/mir-opt/instsimplify/ub_check.rs`, compiled with `//@ compile-flags: -Cdebug-assertions=no -Zinline-mir`, emitting `// EMIT_MIR ub_check.unwrap_unchecked.InstSimplify.diff`. Use an inlined `Option::unwrap_unchecked` path and assert `// CHECK-NOT: UbChecks()`, then `// CHECK: [[assume:_.*]] = const false;`, `// CHECK-NEXT: assume([[assume]]);`. Also construct a companion crate-level `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]` case and verify the `UbChecks()` assignment is retained, since the negative/guard condition is the semantic core. Do not claim execution; these are source- and emitted-MIR-based checks.
analysis.trigger: InstSimplify visits a statement of the form `_x = UbChecks();` (i.e. `StatementKind::Assign` whose RHS is `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, _)`) and the current crate is not marked with `#![rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`.
